title: Run It Yourself: Laptop CPU, Free Colab or a Short GPU Rental
summary: Everything in parts 1 to 5 of the companion repo runs on an ordinary laptop with no GPU; only part 4's 57.9M-parameter default run is worth moving to a free Colab or Kaggle T4. This lesson sizes each part's memory and time from its real configs, sets up a CPU-only environment on Windows, macOS and Linux, runs the repo on Colab with checkpoints on Drive, and shows what Colab Pro or an hour of rented GPU costs.
objectives: Estimate a training run's memory as 16 bytes per parameter plus activations that scale with B·n, and its time as 6·N·tokens divided by achieved throughput
Set up a CPU-only Python 3.11 environment by installing the CPU PyTorch wheel before the repo's pinned requirements, and run every part from its own folder
Run the repo on Google Colab or Kaggle with mixed precision, keep checkpoints on Drive, and resume a run after a disconnect
Convert Colab compute units and rental prices into a cost per run, including setup and idle time, and follow a checklist that avoids paying for idle pods
Work through parts 1 to 5 in order with a specific check for each, starting from a first loss close to ln V
prerequisites: Basic use of a terminal and Python. The memory accounting builds on [Training at scale](/learn/training-and-adaptation/training-at-scale) (16 bytes per parameter) and the parameter counts on [The Transformer Block](/learn/model-foundations/transformer-block), but each topic restates what it needs. You need a copy of the `llm_from_scratch` repo folder on your computer.
